business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Trade Intermediary and Commercial Re-Invoicing Operations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (as amended by Ley 20/2021 and Royal Decree 304/2014)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent from home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Spanish Guardia Civil PEP list, EU sanctions, UN sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and domestic adverse media checks

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (via Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad y Mercantil)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish language required; Latin script only; no transliteration for non-Latin names
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words reserved for public entities (e.g., Banco, Caja, Ayuntamiento), offensive words, or names confusing with existing registered companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name is rejected, file administrative appeal within one month to the Ministry of Justice or relevant registrar authority

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for SL companies if the registered office is a professional address (e.g., business center or serviced office) that complies with commercial substance requirements; not a private residence
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (under 10% for routine AML checks); unannounced inspections possible but rare for new incorporations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC); Articles 20-23 (incorporation formalities), Article 27 (registered office), Articles 102-105 (minimum capital), Articles 209-211 (administrator appointment); supplemented by Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial where the registered office is located, coordinated with the Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) for name reservation; electronic filing via the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) / CIRCE portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarial deed of incorporation) followed by Inscripción en el Registro Mercantil (commercial registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) requires a minimum subscribed and fully paid-up share capital of EUR 3,000 under Article 4 LSC. The full capital must be paid into a bank account opened in the company's name prior to notarization; a bank deposit certificate must be annexed to the deed. No statutory escrow account is mandated, but a notarial deposit or blocked account certification is customary for electronic formation. In-kind contributions require an independent expert valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The founding partners hereby incorporate a private limited liability company (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) under the name certified by the Mercantile Registry and adopt the attached bylaws. (2) The entire share capital of EUR 3,000 is subscribed and fully paid in, as evidenced by the bank deposit certificate. (3) The registered office is fixed at Calle de Alcalá 21, 28014 Madrid. (4) [Full Name] is appointed sole administrator for an indefinite term with all powers under the bylaws. (5) The administrator is expressly authorized to sign the public deed, obtain the Tax Identification Number, register with the Mercantile Registry and Social Security, apply for all licenses and permits, and open corporate bank accounts as necessary to perfect the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Corporate Name and Obtaining Negative Name Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) via electronic filing through the Ministry of Justice online portal or the CIRCE / VUE system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online application 'Solicitud de Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social' with one to three proposed corporate names. Pay the statutory fee electronically. Within the stated SLA, the RMC will issue a 'Certificación Negativa' confirming no identical conflicting company name exists. This certificate is valid for six months and must be attached to the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Form ANV (application for negative name certification)
List of up to three proposed corporate names in order of preference
Identification data (DNI / NIE / Passport) of all founding partners
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RMC rejects the name for identity or similarity with an existing registered name, the applicant may immediately resubmit with alternatives; alternatively, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Ministry of Justice within one month, or a new name will be selected without additional cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital and Obtaining Bank Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish credit institution authorized by the Bank of Spain, or a notary operating a deposit account for formation purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the company 'in formation' and deposit the full statutory minimum capital of EUR 3,000. Request a 'Certificado de Saldo y Depósito' from the bank evidencing the amount, date and payee. For non-cash contributions, obtain an independent expert valuation. The certificate will be annexed to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate from the RMC
Draft bylaws (Estatutos Sociales) including capital allocation
Identity documents of all subscribers
Bank deposit certificate (or independent valuation report for in-kind contributions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the deposit certificate due to AML enquiries, provide the requested beneficial ownership documentation; if unresolved, transfer the funds to another institution and obtain a fresh certificate. A notarial deposit may be substituted, in which case the notary's certificate is used.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Spanish notary public (Notaría) within the notarial district of the company's registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators or their attorneys-in-fact must appear before the notary, present the required dossiers and confirm legal capacity. The notary reviews the name certificate, bank deposit certificate, share capital legality and the draft bylaws. The notary then reads the deed and bylaws, obtains shareholder signatures and issues the public deed. The notary also transmits the deed to the Mercantile Registry and handles the transfer tax (AJD) filing.
required_dossiers: Certificación Negativa del Nombre
Bank deposit certificate (Certificado de Depósito)
Draft bylaws (Estatutos Sociales)
Passport / DNI / NIE for each incorporator
Power of attorney (if signing by representative) with apostille or legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authorization due to a defect (e.g., expiry of the name certificate or capital payment deficiency), cure the technical defect (obtain a new name certificate or supplemental deposit certificate) and hold a new notarial appointment. If a substantive legal defect exists, amend the bylaws and re-execute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registry Registration and Obtaining Provisional/Definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (location of the registered office) and the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary electronically files the deed with the Mercantile Registry. Once the registry examines and inscribes the company, it issues an official registration certificate. In parallel, apply to the AEAT for a provisional NIF using Modelo 036, submitting a notarial copy of the deed. After registration is completed, submit the registration certificate to AEAT to obtain the definitive NIF. File the mandatory censal declaration (036) at this stage.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (first authorized copy)
Provisional NIF application (Modelo 036)
Registration certificate from the Mercantile Registry (for definitive NIF)
Identity document of the legal representative
Authorized appointment as administrator (from the board resolution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Mercantile Registry suspends or rejects the registration, identify the legal defect in the registration notice, prepare a correction deed or auxiliary private document, and resubmit for inscription. If AEAT declines the provisional NIF, correct the Modelo 036 or provide updated incorporation evidence; if a definitive NIF is delayed, the provisional NIF remains valid for banking operations pending resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration, Social Security and Municipal Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS), and the local Ayuntamiento (municipal authority).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete registration with the TGSS to obtain a Código de Cuenta de Cotización (CCC) where any staff will be engaged. File the final Modelo 036 to update the company's address and activity codes. Obtain a digital certificate (FNMT) for electronic filings. If the company occupies physical premises for its re-invoicing business, submit the municipal 'licencia de actividad' / 'comunicación previa' with available building and fire safety documentation. No industrial permit is required for pure commercial intermediation.
required_dossiers: Certification of registration from the Mercantile Registry
Definitive NIF certificate from AEAT
Modelo 036 updates
Lease or ownership title of the physical premises (if any)
Fire safety certificate and basic workplace risk assessment (PRL) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TGSS rejects the CCC registration, verify that the administrators have valid DNI/NIE and that the company is fully registered; correct any data mismatch. If the Ayuntamiento objects to or conditionally licenses the premises, appeal or provide supplementary documentation within 10 days; rely on the Services Directive (2006/123/EC) for light administrative authorization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No specific industrial licensing board is applicable for a pure re-invoicing trade (ISIC 4690). If physical premises are established, the competent municipal authority is the Ayuntamiento (for activity license) and the regional Consejería de Medio Ambiente (for any environmental controls).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for the re-invoicing hub activity. For any office or warehouse presence, the relevant municipal permit is 'Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento' or 'Comunicación Previa' under the Spanish Services Directive.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) in coordination with the environmental agency of the autonomous community (e.g., Consejería de Medio Ambiente de la Comunidad de Madrid).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Estado de Impacto Ambiental report under Ley 21/2013 for pure commercial re-invoicing and office activity. Administrative registration may be required for premises with minor local impacts (e.g., municipal environmental activity registration), but no full EIA for this scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions arise from the re-invoicing activity. Standard municipal wastewater discharge via sewer is permitted subject to local ordinances. For any storage or packaging operation, compliance with Real Decreto 1055/2022 (packaging waste) and municipal waste disposal rules is required. No atmospheric emissions thresholds apply absent equipment or processing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance: premises must comply with Real Decreto 2267/2004 (if industrial/warehouse) or Real Decreto 314/2006 (CTE-DB-SI) for fire-structural behavior. Structural load inspections follow the Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE-DB-SE). Occupational health and safety clearance requires a risk assessment under Ley 31/1995 and provision of training and emergency measures. Municipal clearance is evidenced through a 'certificado de aptitud' or acknowledgment of the 'comunicación previa' from the local authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the statutory TIN is the NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal), obtained automatically upon incorporation at the Commercial Registry and verification through the AEAT. For a foreign entity without a permanent establishment in Spain, the procedure is to appoint a fiscal representative (if required), submit Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios/Profesionales) or Form 037, together with a power-of-attorney and identity documents, to the competent AEAT office, following which the entity is assigned a provisional NIF-IVA (VAT registration number) or definitively registered as a taxable person. The application must be made prior to the commencement of any taxable activity in Spain; for EU entities, the NIF-IVA may also be sought through the VIES exchange procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box or general hybrid-mismatch election. The SL is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at a general rate of 25% (reduced rates apply to newly created entities: 15% for two tax periods and for certain small enterprises). Elective mechanisms available under Spanish tax law include: (i) election for the VAT cash-basis regime (criterio de caja) for small and medium-sized enterprises; (ii) election for group VAT registration under the Special Group VAT Regime (régimen especial de grupo de IVA); (iii) election for a reduced tax-incentive regime for qualifying newly created entities; and (iv) election for consolidated corporate tax grouping under the Spanish consolidated tax group regime. No pass-through election is available for an SL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 - no general statutory turnover threshold for VAT registration; any taxable person undertaking business activities in Spain must register before commencement. For intra-EU distance sales of goods and to-whom supply of electronically supplied services to non-taxable persons, Spain applies the EU-wide EUR 10,000 calendar-year registration threshold across the EU (unless optional taxability in Spain is elected). For wholesale/re-invoicing trade, registration is compulsory upon the first taxable supply or acquisition of goods in Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates B2B electronic invoicing in compliance with the Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) for all entrepreneurs and professionals, with phased implementation after the regulatory development of VeriFactu (fiscal custody system) by AEAT. Large enterprises (annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.20) must file real-time VAT ledger data through the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system using XML/API submission for each invoice; all businesses will be required to issue e-invoices with VeriFactu's QR-code digital stamping and custody, and clearance through AEAT-approved software. Non-resident VAT-registered entities are equally required to preserve and submit SII records when their turnover exceeds the threshold. Triangular and re-invoicing transactions must also comply with the EU OSS/IOSS procedures where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spain to any destination outside the EU are automatically zero-rated (exempt with entitlement to deduction) provided the physical export is completed and evidenced. Zero-rating also applies to intra-EU supplies to VAT-registered customers (with the recipient's valid EU VAT number and EC-sales list reporting), and to certain B2B services supplied to taxable persons established outside the EU (place of supply in the customer's jurisdiction) and services directly related to exported goods, such as loading, transport, and handling, when attributable to the export. For a commercial re-invoicing hub under ISIC 4690, zero-rating is available only when the goods are physically dispatched from Spanish territory; tripartite or chain transactions must be documented to satisfy EU simplified rules (Article 141 of the VAT Directive) or to demonstrate that the first supplier physically exports the goods; otherwise, local 21% VAT applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR (road transport) evidencing dispatch from Spanish/EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank or payment service provider proof of foreign currency inflow demonstrating export settlement)
Proof of owner's identity and customs representation authorization (if applicable)
EC Sales List (when intra-EU zero-rated supply is claimed)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT strictly audits zero-rating claims by cross-checking customs export data, transport documents, bank records, and VAT returns. Fraudulent or inaccurate zero-rating claims trigger: (i) a tax assessment with retroactive clawback of the unpaid VAT for up to four years from the assessment deadline, plus statutory late interest; (ii) penalty surcharges ranging from 50% to 100% of the unpaid VAT amount depending on the degree of concealment and cooperation; (iii) if the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 in one tax period, criminal tax fraud liability under Article 305 of the Código Penal may be imposed, with penalties including imprisonment between two and six years as well as fines; and (iv) loss of entitlement to export zero-rating, exclusion from AEAT's trusted-trader programs, and potential administrative closure during repeated non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the European System of Central Banks; complementary authority for foreign investment and exchange reporting is exercised by the Secretariat of State for Commerce (Secretaría de Estado de Comercio) through the Foreign Investment Registry (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain, as a euro-area member, maintains full convertibility for both capital and current account transactions under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no residual exchange controls on the settlement of trade, repatriation of dividends, or liquidation proceeds for EU/EEA or third-country investors, subject to standard tax withholding and AML reporting. Dividends and profit remittances may be freely transferred once the SL has settled corporate tax (IS) and applicable withholding taxes; treaty-reduced rates may apply upon submission of Spanish tax forms (e.g., Form 210/216/240). Foreign direct investment from non-EU sources may require ex-post declaration to the Foreign Investment Registry, and investments in sectors critical to public security are subject to prior screening under Royal Decree-Law 11/2020. Balance-of-payments reporting obligations to Banco de España arise for any conversion or cross-border transfer exceeding €10,000 per operation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory exchange conversion, or restrictive repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may hold invoiced foreign currency in domestic or authorised non-resident accounts without a forced conversion to EUR. However, all export and import transactions must be supported by the Single Administrative Document (SAD/EXA) filed with the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) for customs and statistical purposes. Cross-border payment receipts and outflows must be declared to Banco de España via the Statistical Declaration of Operations (Form T1/T3) at or above the €10,000 threshold; failure to submit carries administrative penalties. Receipts related to re-invoicing activities should reference the underlying commercial invoices and the applicable ISIC/NACE code to avoid being categorised as financial flows.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (Electronic Money Institutions) are viable for the SL only if they hold a valid EU/EEA EMI licence and are registered with the Bank of Spain for cross-border provision of payment services under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) or Article 5 of Royal Decree-Law 19/2018. An offshore non-EU EMI without a passporting licence is not acceptable for treasury operations. Feasibility rating: Medium-High for an EU-licensed EMI (e.g., operating from Lithuania or Germany) that supports multi-currency IBANs and SWIFT/SEPA; Legal constraints include: (i) the obligation to maintain a Spanish bank account for corporate income tax and VAT filings (AEAT requires a domestic EUR account or a designated agent), (ii) banks may reject deposits from an unregistered EMI, (iii) enhanced AML due diligence is triggered by trade intermediary flows, and (iv) the EMI cannot provide credit facilities or cash-custody services beyond e-money limits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated SL with non-resident ownership, Spanish AML Law 10/2010 mandates robust customer due diligence. In practice, a physical appearance by at least one director or a duly authorised representative (holding a notarised power of attorney) is normally required at the Spanish bank branch for signing the account mandate and completing KYC verification. Remote opening via qualified electronic signature (eIDAS) and video conference is technically permitted but rarely approved for medium-risk re-invoicing entities unless the bank's compliance committee grants an exemption. We therefore recommend scheduling an in-person kickoff interview at the chosen bank's commercial or private-banking office, with original constitutional documents and UBO proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed SL with immediate high-volume cross-border wiring activity and no local physical warehouse or inventory, creating a perceived pass-through risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución); audited or management-prepared business plan; proof of registered office and operational premises (lease agreement, utility invoices); group organisational chart and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration; signed master framework agreements with related-party suppliers and buyers; historic/forwarding trade flow reconciliation with commercial invoices and purchase orders; and a written compliance memorandum demonstrating that the SL performs genuine re-invoicing and assumes inventory/credit risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or receipts from FATF-grey-listed or high-risk third-country jurisdictions (e.g., certain South American or Middle Eastern states) lacking transparent end-beneficiary information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade documentation pack per transaction, including commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/airway bill, and customs declaration (SAD); full sanctions and PEP screening results against UN/EU/OFAC lists; correspondent-bank account details with regulatory references; a tailored country risk assessment and AML analysis of the counterparty; end-beneficiary affidavits from the overseas purchasing entity; and a copy of the commercial contract term sheet with payment milestones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate frequency of FX conversions or stated reliance on cash-equivalent instruments (e.g., e-wallets, prepaid cards, or cryptocurrency) contradicting the declared trade intermediary business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed source-of-wealth and funds report compiling the SL's full current-account statements, complete ledger of receivable/payable invoices, payment gateway settlement reports, and tax filings; notarised declarations from each material counterparty verifying trade purpose; documentary evidence of any third-party funding (shareholder loan agreements or debenture); and, on request, a forensic accountant's assurance opinion on the economic substance and legality of the FX transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections to the Spanish SL must be executed via wire transfer (MT103) or SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR, with the sending party strictly matching the registered shareholder's legal name and domicile. The bank requires a notarised capital-increase deed (escritura de aumento de capital) or a shareholder loan agreement, evidenced by a signed Board resolution and loan terms. The transfer must reference a clear purpose code (e.g., 'FDI-EQUITY' or 'Loan/Shareholder Advance') for the Banco de España statistical declaration; on receipt, Treasury must file Form T1/T3 and, when applicable, the ex-post foreign investment declaration. If the contribution exceeds €3,005,065.08 from a non-EU investor, a prior authorisation may be necessary for sectors subject to Royal Decree-Law 11/2020; for general re-invoicing (NACE 4690) prior authorisation is not automatic but should be screened with the Foreign Investment Registry. No minimum capital escrow is statutorily required for an SL, though the bank may internally require a minimum deposit (often €3,000–€6,000) to activate the relationship.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the re-invoicing hub will be cleared through three principal rails: (1) SEPA/SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EUR disbursements to EU/EEA beneficiaries up to the SEPA transaction limit; (2) SWIFT MT103/103+ for non-EEA wired payments, with TARGET2 clearing for euro legs and correspondent-banking for USD/GBP/CNH legs; and (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits) for transactional or high-value settlements (typically above €200,000) in higher-risk geographies. Each disbursement instruction must attach the relevant trade documents, customs reference (if applicable), and a statement of beneficial ownership; for jurisdictions with local currency controls, the underlying contract and a valid purpose code (e.g., 'Trade in Goods') must be filed with the paying bank. The treasury system must maintain an immutable payment record, including exchange-rate quotation and SWIFT UETR tracking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Outright Forward Contracts (single-date forwards) with maturities up to 18 months, conducted under an ISDA Master Agreement or the Spanish Master Agreement for Financial Transactions (Acuerdo Marco Español), with a Banco de España-supervised counterparty.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to capital controls (e.g., Argentine peso, South African rand) through the interbank market, executed only with authorised credit institutions and documented via a nontransferable NDF schedule.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for hedging the currency risk and interest rate basis on shareholder loans (e.g., EURIBOR vs. USD SOFR), allowing the SL to convert entire cash-flow streams into a single functional currency.
Spot FX facilities allowing same-day settlement and monetisation of export receivables; although not strictly hedging, these are essential liquidity tools.

Option-based collars or purchased FX options (costless collar structure) for uncertain re-invoicing flows in volatile emerging-markets currencies, subject to bank credit approval and the suitability assessment under MiFID II.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors must prepare accounts within three months after year-end; shareholders must approve them within six months after year-end; filing is due within one month after approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure may prevent registration of most corporate acts; late filing may result in fines of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, increased for larger turnover, and failure to file for one year may trigger registry closure and possible administrative dissolution measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year company, normally 1 to 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without tax payable generally attracts fixed or percentage penalties; unpaid tax generates interest and collection surcharges, with additional penalties for tax understatements or non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return, Modelo 390, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due from 1 to 30 January for the preceding calendar year; certain taxpayers are exempt from filing where qualifying periodic VAT reporting applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing may result in fixed tax penalties, increased for repeated or materially incorrect reporting; unpaid VAT is subject to interest and collection surcharges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounting and corporate books must generally be submitted electronically for legalization within four months after the close of the financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late legalization can impair evidentiary value of books and may contribute to sanctions for accounting non-compliance; registry filing restrictions may arise where related statutory filings are also deficient.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration accompanying annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO information is generally confirmed or updated in the beneficial ownership declaration filed with the annual accounts; material ownership or control changes must be reflected through the applicable notarial and registry channels without delay.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect, incomplete, or outdated beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry restrictions, and administrative sanctions under Spanish anti-money laundering legislation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of these three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce of more than 50 employees. Audit requirements also apply in specified regulated, public-interest, group, or other statutory circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish accounting legislation; IFRS is generally required for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may apply in other legally permitted circumstances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain has no separate annual confirmation statement equivalent to the United Kingdom filing. The company must maintain current beneficial ownership information, report qualifying changes through the applicable notarial or Mercantile Registry mechanisms, and include the required beneficial ownership declaration with the annual accounts filing. Share transfers must be documented and recorded in the private Register of Members; the company must update UBO information when control changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-1,800 annually, depending on address, mail handling, nominee or representative services, and compliance support; Spain does not impose a separate annual registered-agent renewal fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,500-6,000 for a small non-complex SL; higher fees apply for regulated entities, groups, significant cross-border transactions, or complex inventory and revenue testing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for newly created entities for the first two years of profitable activity (subject to conditions). Tax credits for R&D&I, export activities, and investment in renewable fixed assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 - Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically via the AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Tributación) online portal (Sede Electrónica).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the 6 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., for calendar year-end, by July 25).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number (NIF) and entity details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must have a Spanish NIF and file via a tax representative if they have a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting result (profit or loss) before adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the accounting result as per Spanish GAAP, adjusted for any permanent establishment income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments to the accounting result (e.g., permanent differences, temporary differences).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all required adjustments, including transfer pricing adjustments and disallowed expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base (after offsetting tax loss carryforwards).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply any available tax loss carryforwards; Spain allows indefinite carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate (standard 25% or reduced 15% for new entities).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the standard rate unless the entity qualifies for the reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability before deductions and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate based on taxable base and rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and tax credits (e.g., double taxation relief, R&D credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty relief for foreign taxes paid, if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refund due.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount if filed within 3 months of the deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 - Quarterly Corporate Income Tax Prepayment Return, filed electronically via AEAT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (first three months of the fiscal year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the first 20 days of the month following the end of each quarter (April 20, July 20, October 20).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with a permanent establishment must file; others are not required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable base for the quarter (based on prior year's tax or actual results).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the method chosen (e.g., 18% of prior year's taxable base).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayment amount (tax rate applied to estimated base).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 25% rate unless reduced rate applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the prepayment amount, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month, and fixed penalty of €200 if no amount due.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident must submit Form 210 (Non-Resident Income Tax) or Form 211 for refund, along with a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the residence state. The TRC must be submitted to the Spanish tax authority or the paying entity to apply the reduced rate at source. Alternatively, a refund can be claimed after the fact.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: Royalties 24%, Interest 19%. Treaty rates may reduce these (e.g., EU Interest and Royalties Directive allows 0% for EU companies under certain conditions).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Entities with net revenue exceeding €10 million must prepare Local File and Master File. Below this threshold, a simplified documentation (summary) is required.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies substance-over-form principles. While there is no specific ESR, the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) and CFC rules require that entities have real economic substance (staff, premises, functions) to justify recharacterization. For re-invoicing hubs, substance is critical to avoid being treated as a shell company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, overstatement of invoices, or fraudulent transfers to avoid tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax evaded, plus administrative interest. Criminal prosecution for amounts exceeding €50,000 per year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 6 years for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a re-invoicing hub without real business activity, employees, or premises, solely to shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, disallowance of deductions, application of CFC rules, and penalty of 50% of the tax avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for unpaid taxes and penalties, and criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, report suspicious transactions, or maintain records as required by Law 10/2010.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 1% of annual turnover, and suspension of business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and banned from managing companies for up to 10 years.
